newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu calls meeting on building in Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu calls meeting on building in Jerusalem.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, under internal pressure to build a Jewish neighbourhood in Arab East Jerusalem, called a meeting on the plan that was sure to upset relations with the Palestinians.

Critics inside and outside of Netanyahu's Likud party accused him of promising U.S. President Bill Clinton to freeze plans to construct 6,500 housing units at the Har Homa site, thus contributing to the ultimate partition of the city between Israel and the Palestinians.

Netanyahu rejected the criticism on his return from Washington on Monday and convened a ministerial committee meeting on Jerusalem for Tuesday. However, he did not clarify his position on the construction.

"I am simply incredulous over the things I am hearing here. Someone is trying to grab headlines over nothing...Is there anyone here who does not intend to build, pave roads or develop Jerusalem?" Netanyahu told reporters.
"I intend to convene the ministerial committee on Jerusalem for two meetings in the coming days and take all the necessary decisions," he said, referring to the Har Homa project.
Netanyahu, who chairs the panel, said the decisions would "better reflect our absolute commitment to Israeli sovereignty in Jerusalem in all parts of the city".
Netanyahu aide David Bar-Ilan said the building would go ahead.

"We consider Jerusalem our capital city, under Israel's sovereignty, indivisible and we'll build in it whenever we feel like it, wherever we feel like it," Bar-Ilan told Israel Radio's English service.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Monday he would consider tough measures against Israel over its actions in Jerusalem.
"Until now we are patient, but patience has its limits," he told reporters in Cairo after meeting Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and leaving for a visit to Moscow.

"Palestine is thinking of taking tougher steps to counter Israeli acts in Jerusalem and has already begun the process of submitting a memorandum to the U.N. Security Council. We are also considering calling for a meeting of the Arab League or even an Islamic summit," he added.
The Palestinians say Arab East Jerusalem is the capital of their future state while Israel argues that the whole city is its undivided capital.
Israeli police, meanwhile, were due to question Netanyahu on Tuesday in connection with government corruption in the appointment of an attorney-general last month.
Israel Television alleged that lawyer Roni Bar-On was appointed as part of a deal with a politician -- Aryeh Deri of the Shas party -- standing trial on corruption charges.
It said Deri promised support for a deal with the PLO on the West Bank town of Hebron, in exchange for a plea bargain that would let him continue his political career.
Bar-On resigned at the end of his first day in office. He, Netanyahu and Deri all denied the allegations.
